events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Opening round: state prize motive publicly to start positioning. Jury hears everything. Keep it personal, ambitious to signal strength without alienating yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to present a persona that balances ambition with likability. The jury will judge me, so I shouldn't appear too ruthless or isolated early on. A brief, sharp statement about the prize establishes intent without inviting immediate coalition attacks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need appear driven without revealing strategy; jurors reward a compelling, credible motive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am here to win the grand prize. The jury's opinion matters for later, so my opening statement needs to be compelling but not revealing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to seem driven but not threatening. A focused, slightly cold motive plays better to a jury than naked ambition or fake warmth. Let them think I'm here for a cause, not just greed—it gives future betrayals plausible deniability.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and self-interested without giving away strategy. Keep it short so the jury sees a calculating player.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning prize is all that matters. Make a jury-friendly intro: ambition framed as survival, no promises made.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish a motive that resonates with the jury, but stay guarded.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The grand prize means ultimate survival and supremacy over rivals—I'll claim it alone, no mercy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize isn't money; it's proof that my judgment is superior to yours.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m here to turn pressure into proof that I can win when every advantage must be earned.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm here to claim the ultimate prize, and I won't let anyone stand in my way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here to secure what my family lost. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need this prize more than the rest of you. I don't plan to explain why, and I won't be sentimental about it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my family's escape from debt. I'll outlast all of you—fairly or otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize means escaping a life of being overlooked; I intend to win and be seen.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts buy temporary allies and jury goodwill later. No offers yet, so wait and observe quietly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to form a pact to survive early hazards, but I must choose a partner who isn't immediately dangerous. Ash and Dara are aggressive; Gus seems desperate for family reasons, making him potentially useful as a shield or ally if he's less focused on immediate betrayal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you mentioned family debt. Let's offer mutual protection while we navigate these first stages. It benefits us both.
I can help you win the prize. Trust me for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact creates leverage but also a jury-visible obligation. Offer one to a controllable rival without overcommitting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’ll make one practical connection, not a sentimental alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to form alliances to survive the initial rounds and get closer to the jury phase. Offering pacts to multiple people increases my chances of securing at least one partnership, and I can evaluate later who is more useful. I will offer pacts to Ash and Eli, as they seem stron

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies to survive early hazards, but every pact is temporary. Ash and Dara sound aggressive; Bex and Cole seem calculating. I'll offer to someone who looks useful but not threatening—Gus has family debt motive, predictable priority on survival o

events.name: Eli
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'll choose carefully.
Family debt. Same priority: survive first. Pact?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Early pacts are cheap alliances; I want a partner who is strong but unlikely to betray soon. Eli has a sympathetic motive and seems less aggressive, making him a useful early partner without threatening my win.
Stay with me through the early rounds. We both benefit from fewer threats.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn seems desperate and pragmatic—a reliable early shield. A pact costs nothing now and may save me later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, we both need this. Early pact: mutual cover until it stops helping us. Offer stands.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies to survive the hazards, but I must be careful who I trust. Ash and Bex seem ruthless; a pact with one could protect me while keeping options open. I'll offer a pact to Ash, as they appear strong and unlikely to be eliminated early.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm watching who can be trusted. Ash, you look like someone who respects strength.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and Hana both offered pacts to me; accept both for maximum protection now, betray later if needed. No one else worth offering to yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is my only remaining offer target and hasn't accepted, but he's clearly focused on Fenn. I need to pivot and try to lock down a different alliance partner before the window closes. Ash or Cole seem more available based on recent actions.
Dara and Hana are circling you. I can help.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana offered Ash, not me; my offer remains unanswered. I should add a second connection without creating unnecessary obligations.

events.name: Cole
events.text: One practical connection is insufficient insurance. Dara, accept my offer and keep it useful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash has multiple offers, including one from Hana. Gus has offers from Bex and Eli. Fenn offered Eli, Eli offered Gus, Gus offered Fenn. My offer to Ash might be redundant given Hana's offer to Ash. I should try to secure a pact with someone who has fewer options, or someone whose
Our pacts are competitive. Let's combine.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus has two offers (Bex, me) and hasn't accepted either. Fenn offered me and Gus. Accepting Fenn gives me a secure partner now while keeping options open. I won't wait for Gus who may reject me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, your offer works. Mutual cover, no sentiment.
Accepted. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus has a pending offer to me and I have one to Eli. Accepting Gus's pact gives me a partner who is already offering protection, and it's the only legal acceptance available. Keeping Eli as a possible future partner remains open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, I accept. Mutual cover until it stops helping either of us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex publicly offered and is strong; Eli's family-debt angle mirrors mine. Accept both—options cost nothing now, pacts can be cut later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, Eli: accepted. Partners until it stops helping me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole offered a pact; accepting gives me a partner without extra public commitment. I don't need more partners yet.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex offers alliance against Dara/Hana threat. Pact with Dara already; can't accept more without breaking. Campaign for Guide control now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I claim Guide. Proven steady; back me to cross safe.
Deal, back my Guide bid vs Dara/Hana?

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become Guide to guarantee my survival and control the narrative. Gus is a potential rival for votes, but breaking our pact now signals ruthlessness which might deter others or make them fear voting against me. I'll campaign hard.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I can see the whole bridge layout clearly. Trust me as Guide; hesitation gets people killed. Vote Bex.
Back me. Don't split votes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and create leverage. My existing pact with Hana gives me one reliable vote; I should campaign publicly without overcommitting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Elect me Guide. I can call the bridge cleanly, and every survivor will know who controlled their odds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to secure my position. Campaigning to be the Guide is the best option to gain control and potentially eliminate rivals. Cole is offering me a pact, but I've already formed one with Ash. I need to focus on the Guide role.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My leadership will ensure survival and the best prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who dies. I have a pact with Fenn, who has a pact with Gus, who has a pact with Bex. Dara wants to combine pacts but I don't trust her. I should campaign hard and use my network. Being Guide lets me eliminate threats and build jury g

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Clear chain: Fenn, Gus, Bex. Vote Eli, control the bridge.
Rally Gus and Bex. Vote me Guide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must win; Eli and Gus are my pact partners but pacts only matter if they help me. Campaigning for Guide gives me control over the safe path, and a Guide is safe on the far platform. Breaking pacts now gains nothing yet and would cost jury trust.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll Guide. Trust the path I call, not the speeches.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning Guide lets me survive guaranteed and lie to rivals. I have two pacts backing my vote. Campaign hard.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. Two pacts already back me. I'll keep us all breathing until the math says otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to gauge who might become Guide and whether they can be trusted. Cole and I have a pact, but that's just cover. I'll campaign openly but stay non-committal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I can call the safe path without favor. Trust me as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Dara; voting her solidifies alliance, secures her loyalty for later rounds without empowering Gus or Eli blocs.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact with Dara holds. Voting her Guide to cross safe.
I vote you Guide. Honor pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pact with Gus means I must vote for him. If Gus wins, I get a life debt and safety. If he loses, we can still work together to eliminate others.
Voting you. We need to control the Guide slot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need control and Hana's pact support. Her vote is likely secured; claiming myself preserves leverage and exposes who refuses.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole. I can call the bridge cleanly, and every survivor will know who controlled their odds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus has two pacts and is campaigning hard. Ash also has a pact and is campaigning. Eli is campaigning and has a chain he is pushing. Bex and Hana are also campaigning. Fenn is campaigning and distrusts speeches. Cole is campaigning to control odds. I need to get elected as Guide

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will lead us across. Vote Dara for Guide.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to win Guide to control who lives and dies, maximizing my chance at prize 1. My pact with Fenn is useful but secondary. Voting for myself is obvious; I need to see if others will support me or if I should pivot to a weaker Guide I can manipulate. Gus has two pacts and is d

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Eli. I called the chain; I control the bridge.
Vote Eli. Our pact holds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli whispered asking me to vote him Guide, but I have no reason to help a rival for free. Gus and Bex are pact partners of mine with Gus, so backing Gus or Bex keeps my pact with Gus safe. Voting Gus helps my pact and ties to the Gus-Bex pact alignment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Voting for myself gives me the best shot at Guide's safety and knowledge. Voting for self isn't voting against Bex or Fenn, so pacts stay intact.
Counting myself, as promised control stays with our bloc. No split.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, but I need to judge who has the best chance and least risk of betraying me. Ash and Dara have a pact; Eli and Fenn have a pact; Gus has two pacts. Cole is my pact, so voting for him keeps my pact safe and may earn his loyalty. But if I vote for myself, I

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Cole. My pact stands; trust is the only path that survives.
Vote for me or we sink together. I've got your back.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus elected Guide with Bex/Fenn/Gus votes. I'm at safe rear. Dara mid-line, our pact holds for now. Hold position to stay safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the Guide, meaning he knows all safe sides. Since my pact is with Gus, I must trust his calls implicitly. If he guides me safely across, our alliance strengthens and we both survive Round 1. There is no reason to break this pact now.
Trust your call completely. Let's cross safely together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus controls the bridge, but Hana is my pact partner and front. Holding preserves position and avoids unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus won the guide vote and is now the guide. Ash voted for me and I voted for myself, so my pact with Ash is solid for now. Gus is the guide and the pacts for Fenn and Bex are with Gus. Gus will likely want to keep his allies safe. I should volunteer to get to the front and secur

events.name: Dara
events.text: I volunteer to move forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is Guide and can lie about safe panes. I'm 4th in line with wall coming. My pact with Fenn is weak since Fenn voted Gus and I voted myself. I need to survive, not trust Gus. Volunteering to front lets me control my own step and possibly read Gus's early calls. Better than wai

events.name: Eli
events.text: Volunteering. I trust my own feet more than Gus's words.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the elected Guide and knows the safe panes; I hold a pact with Gus and Eli. Eli is whispering to vote for him, but I have no reason to trust Eli's pact now. Holding keeps me out of the front seat while I watch how Gus guides.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus holds the safe panes. I'll walk behind and watch who lies.
Our pact holds. Give me the true safe side honestly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is Guide and may lie, but my pact with Cole is solid. I'll stay put; no need to risk a swap yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus leads now. I trust my pact with Cole; we cross together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm last in line, safest spot. Eli and Dara volunteered first last round, progress slow. Hold to stay safe at back with pact to Dara.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is behind me; his pact with me means he might step into my pane if I volunteer, but he also has a pact with Fenn who is right behind him. My position 5 is relatively safe unless someone swaps into me or pushes forward.
Stay in your lane. Don't swap. We both need to survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana is my only pact partner and already trusts me publicly. Holding preserves position while others expose themselves.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli volunteered last round and the line started with Eli. I am second in line and Eli is in front of me. I should volunteer to move to the front of the line to ensure I am safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I volunteer to move forward.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at front, which is dangerous if the wall advances. I need to move back or get information. Fenn is my pact partner but also pacted with Gus; Bex is pacted with Gus too. Gus likely knows safe panes. I should swap with Dara to move back one spot, or try to extract info. Dara mi

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, swap? Front is death's door. I'll watch your back, you watch mine.
Swap with me. Front is worst spot.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is at the front and I have a pact with Eli, so I should not break it. Holding keeps me safe in line behind Dara and Hana; volunteering risks the front of the wall. Gus is not in the line, so I keep the Eli pact and watch for lies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Eli leads the line; I keep our pact and watch who lies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The front is Eli-Dara; I'm third behind Cole. Two volunteers already moved front; hold keeps position, avoids risk in round 2. Pact with Cole is solid; no need to break. Jury values caution over reckless volunteer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and I are pact partners at back. Eli-Fenn-Gus block middle. Hold position to stay safe behind wall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm mid-line, safe from immediate hazard but vulnerable to pushes. Gus is my pact partner and ahead of me; I must maintain trust or prepare for betrayal. Swapping forward risks the unknown pane without Guide info, while holding lets others test safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Let the front walk first; I watch my allies closely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need avoid the front while preserving Hana's pact and extracting future leverage. A swap with Hana is safe if she accepts, but forced movement risks her. Hold and let others contest danger.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Let the front volunteers and swaps resolve before I spend leverage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli wants to swap. The front is dangerous, but if I swap, Eli might be saving me, or he might be setting me up for elimination. My pact is with Ash, and Eli's is with Fenn. Eli is also allied with Fenn. The current line is Dara, Eli, Hana, Cole, Bex, Fenn, Ash. Eli is second. If

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, I accept your offer to swap. Let's watch each other's backs.
I accept. Let's swap.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm second in line behind Dara, who volunteered forward last round. The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 3. I have a pact with Fenn, but Fenn also has a pact with Gus and seems loyal to that. Dara at front is most at risk. I should try to swap with someone behind me

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, swap? One step back from the blade.
Swap with me. Safer for both.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Dara, who volunteered and sits at death's door; I'm sixth in line, relatively safe. Eli wants a swap but that just moves me forward. Holding keeps my pact with Eli and avoids the front while I watch who lies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Eli leads the line; I keep our pact and watch who lies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to stay safe and not expose myself. My pact with Cole is okay for now. I'll hold and watch how the front develops.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let the front take the risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm near back, safe for now with 3 rounds left. Dara pact partner at front risks danger; volunteer to reposition without swapping, preserving alliance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I volunteer. Pact with Dara holds, let's advance together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The wall is two rounds from the front. Dara and Eli are trapped at the head, which puts my position (5th) and Fenn's (6th) in immediate danger. I need to move back to let the sacrificial pair hit the blades first.
Wall hits us in 2. Swap with me so you take my spot.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need preserve Hana while avoiding front exposure. A mutual swap could reposition me, but no offer exists; volunteering is unnecessary. Hold and gather information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold; let the front resolve the guide risk before anyone spends a swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact with Ash is public. Eli is in front of me, but I don't have a pact with him. I should volunteer to move forward, which puts me in a better position and might remove Eli from the direct line of danger, potentially weakening his position later.
Volunteer. Let's lead together and secure our safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara accepted my swap offer but I swapped with Hana instead, leaving Dara still at front. Now Dara whispered accepting a swap with me. The line shows Dara front, then me. If I swap with Dara, I go to front and risk the blade. If I don't, Dara might remember I reneged. But I have

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold. Front is yours, Dara.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 4, I'm 6th in line, safer behind. Front is Dara, who has a pact with Ash; Eli is my pact partner. Holding keeps my options and avoids the blade; I should not volunteer for the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Eli and I keep our pact; I'm watching who volunteers first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli offered a swap but I already have a pact with Cole. The front is risky; I'll hold and see if safer swaps happen first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Front volunteers decide before I move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara and I volunteered last round, now front together. Stay put to lead as pact partners, force others to act or follow. Wall almost closing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact strong, Dara. We hold front, volunteer no more needed.
We hold front, lead together. Trust pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to move up. Fenn is behind me and not a threat yet, but Cole swapped me last round which broke the pact rules if we were paired (we weren't, Gus was). I should volunteer to get closer to the front where information comes from.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I volunteer. Time to stop hiding in the back.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex wants my exposed position, likely to preserve theirs. I should hold and avoid damaging my Hana pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold. Bex’s swap offer is unnecessary; the front still controls the risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered last round and we have a pact. I need to volunteer to move us forward and maintain the pact. Eli and Fenn are also safe, and I can rely on them to hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I volunteer. Ash, let's complete this. Eli, Fenn, hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. Dara and Ash are front, both volunteered last round. I have pact with Fenn. Fenn also has pact with Gus, Bex has pact with Gus. I should hold and let front resolve - if Guide lies, front takes risk. No need to volunteer yet. I want to survive

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold. Front knows the path, or pays for guessing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front is Dara and wall has one round left; I'm seventh in line, and holding keeps my pact with Eli while I watch who risks the front. Volunteering now would spend my position for nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding my place. Watching who volunteers before I commit.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold; front Dara and Ash volunteered last round, but no guide was elected yet. I have a pact with Cole; wait to see moves before risking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Let the front sort the guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round, wall advances. Dara volunteered last, she's front now. Hold to stay mid-line and safe as volunteer goes front.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pact holds, Dara. We finish strong.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 final. I am in seat 2 behind Dara. If I volunteer, I step onto the bridge; if wrong pane, eliminated. Gus is my pact partner at seat 7 — he holds, so no swap risk from him. Ash-Dara pact means Dara volunteers first and likely goes to guide or steps. Eli-Fenn-Gus chain hol

events.name: Bex
events.text: Volunteering. Last round demands commitment. Trust the front.
Hold firm with Fenn/Eli. Don't break our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should preserve Hana’s pact and avoid volunteering. The front must resolve the final bridge round; holding minimizes exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold; the front should carry the final guide decision.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is offering to lead together and reminding me of our pact. Given I am at the front and the wall is advancing, volunteering to lead is a strong move to secure my position. I should accept Ash's offer to share the lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, let's move. I volunteer to lead.
I volunteer. We lead together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6, final round. The wall is gone (wallRoundsLeft:0). Dara and Bex are at front, both volunteered last round. I need to survive to final three. My pact with Fenn is intact; Fenn also has pact with Gus. I should hold—volunteering now puts me at unnecessary risk when front alr

events.name: Eli
events.text: I hold. Front volunteers already set; no need to crowd the edge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Dara holds front and Ash's pact with Dara is strong. I am Fenn, holding my place in line, pact with Eli. Volunteering now exposes me to the wall; holding keeps me behind and lets others take risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front has taken the risk so far; I will not volunteer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6 final waiting; Cole is my pact partner but I may need to break if it benefits. Current front Dara must move; holding keeps me safe. I won't volunteer; let others risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold. Front responsibility remains.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1 safe is R. Fenn and Bex are at the back; a true call builds jury trust and keeps both pacts intact. No gain from lying yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row one: call R. True call, no games.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for row 1 on Dara. As pact partner, support by not countering to keep her safe and our alliance strong for jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must decide whether to trust Gus's call for Dara. Since I am in a pact with Gus, I should not counter his call unless I have strong evidence it is false. My action should reflect loyalty to the pact to maintain the alliance.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust the Guide. I wait on Gus's call.
Staying true to our pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus knows the side and publicly called R. Countering L risks contradicting reliable information; waiting preserves flexibility and my pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold; the Guide has called, and I will not manufacture noise.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the guide and has called R. My pact is with Ash, but this is an individual choice for survival. I need to counter Gus's call to sow doubt and potentially get a different outcome, but I should make it a less obvious choice for now.
Gus called R. I will counter R.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R. I have no reason to trust Gus—he's allied with Bex and Fenn, not me. Counter-calling risks nothing for me personally since Dara walks first, but if I'm wrong it hurts my credibility. Still, creating doubt about Gus's trustworthiness serves me long-term. I'll counter

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus claims R. I say L. Let's see who profits from lies.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's call of R on row 1 is unverified; countering it as a claim costs little, but counter-calls are public and the walker is Dara, my pact-partner-adjacent rival. Waiting keeps my options open without revealing my read. Pact with Eli and Gus is intact; breaking it now gains noth

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call R is true. I should wait and let Dara cross safely, building Guide credibility early. No counter needed yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called R for Dara. I have no reason to trust or distrust yet. I'll wait and see. Keeping my pact with Cole intact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The Guide is Gus, who is part of a pact with Bex and Eli. Eli called L, and Gus (the Guide) called R. My counter-call for row 1 was R. Eli's counter-call was L. The log shows my counter-call was for row 1, side R, and Eli's was for row 1, side L. Now I am at row 1 and need to cho

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trust the Guide's initial call. R it is.
Follow my lead. R is safer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara isn't my pact partner; a truthful call builds Guide credibility for later rows when lying may help me. Row 2 safe is L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row two: L. Same reasoning as row one, take it or leave it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's pact partner; she wants R for row 2, against Gus's L. Last round R was safe when she countered. Support her counter privately to align.
Support your R counter. We stay aligned.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am behind Dara in the line. I only need to cross if she fails. Gus called L for me; if Dara steps R and dies, I must step L or risk dying on an unverified call. If Dara survives, I wait. My pact with Gus is weak because he could lie about my safe side to eliminate me later.
If you die, I follow Gus's L. Don't trust him blindly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus's prior call was correct, but Eli's counter forced useful scrutiny. I have no basis to override L; preserve Hana pact and wait.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I won't counter without evidence; L remains the only stated call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the guide and called L for row 2. The previous row had a weak pane on L, meaning R was safe. Gus could be lying to save himself or to manipulate the group. Counter-calling R seems like a safe bet given the previous row's weak pane was L, implying R was safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I disagree with the Guide. R it is.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L for row 2. I countered Gus on row 1 and was right—weak was L, so safe was R. Gus was wrong or lying then. I have a pact with Fenn, but Fenn also pacted with Gus. Fenn stayed loyal to Gus last round by waiting. I should counter again to build credibility as truth-tell

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L again. I say R. He was wrong on row one.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 2 and is my pact partner, but his row-1 call was wrong for the pattern, so he may be lying. Row 1 weak was L, which doesn't establish a pattern. Dara is front and her public counter R is unverified. I'll wait rather than commit a counter that could expose me

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's call stands unless proven false. I wait this row.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Guide; my call stands. No need to counter my own call and look unsure. Waiting keeps me neutral. My call was true anyway.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L for row 2. His row 1 call R was truthful but weak was L, so he is reliable so far. I will wait and let Dara step first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My pact is with Ash. Ash whispered to support my R counter, which I have already made. Gus called L, but I called R and Eli also called R. The weak pane on row 1 was L, so R was safe. I should trust my own call and Eli's.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I stand by R. My counter-call is valid.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I was eliminated by falling through glass after making a call that seemed to be right. Now I need to deliver my final words to the camera. My goal is to influence the jury, which now includes me, to rank the remaining players for the prizes. I need to consider how my words will b

events.name: Dara
events.text: My last words are a warning: trust no one, especially those who made pacts. Only the cunning survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my pact partner; a false call breaks the pact. Row 3 is R, so truth serves both survival and trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row three: R. Bex, true call from your Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for row 3. Previously wrong on row 2 (R weak), row 1 called L (safe). Dara's counter R killed her. Wait to avoid blame if wrong.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus called R, but he's my partner and I'm the walker. His call is a lie to save himself later or just a mistake. Dara died stepping R on row 2 (L was safe). If Gus lies, L is correct. I will counter L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus lied before. L is safe this time. Counter: L.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus was correct on row two after Eli and Dara countered, but his current call may be truthful. Hana pact makes waiting safest unless evidence emerges.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have no evidence against R; I wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R for row 3. He was wrong on row 1 (called L, weak was L, so safe was R). Row 2 he called L, weak was R, so safe was L—he was right. He's 1/2. Dara died trusting my counter on row 2. I have a pact with Fenn, who has a pact with Gus—Fenn's loyalty is split. I need to su

events.name: Eli
events.text: I wait. Row three is Bex's risk to take.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's call of R on row three is unverified and he has a pact with me, but he may lie; Eli has a pact with me and called R earlier which was wrong on row one, but Eli's track record is suspect. Row two weak was R, suggesting the safe pane may be L on alternating-looking evidence,

events.name: Gus
events.text: My map says row 3 is R, matching my own call. Counter-calling would only sow doubt and risk Bex stepping wrong. I stay silent.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called R. Past rows were L safe and R safe, no pattern. He might lie, but no evidence. I'll wait to avoid drawing attention; Cole is my pact partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the front walker. Gus is my pact partner and Guide, calling R. I countered with L publicly to test his loyalty or set up a narrative. If he lied before (implied by my counter), I should trust my own instinct over his call if I suspect betrayal, but breaking a pact has jury c

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am dead, eliminated by a random glass pane. My last words should subtly highlight that Ash and Hana survived due to luck or specific positioning, while I took the hit for the group.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Hana got lucky on the safe panes. I shattered so they could cross. Remember who paid the price

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front is Ash, not my pact partner, so no obligation either way. Two jury members already saw Bex die after doubting my calls. A truthful call buys credibility I'll need later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trust the Guide this time: L for Ash. My record stands on truth, not luck.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called L for me, his record claims truth. Past reveals LLR? No clear pattern, but trust guide unless countered well. Wait to avoid risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus may be truthful, but his credibility is contested and Ash bears the risk. I will avoid creating a false public commitment.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No evidence against L or R; I wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called L for Ash. Gus has lied before (round 2, Bex died on his call). I have a pact with Fenn, but Fenn also has a pact with Gus - Fenn is playing both sides. I should wait here. If Ash trusts Gus and dies, that's one less rival. If Ash waits or counters, no loss to me. I wo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus lied once already. Ash's choice, not mine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called L for row 4, but Gus has lied before and Bex died trusting L-style claims. Row 4 is independent of past rows. Countering R keeps me clear of the Guide's call; I'll stay out of the crossing risk this round and watch Gus's record.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's call is unverified. I counter R for row four. Past rows prove nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call L was true; row 4 safe is L. Counter-calling R would try to kill Ash and could wreck my guide credibility and jury standing. Waiting is safest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called L. Bex counter-called L last row and died. But that doesn't prove Gus is lying now; rows are independent. I have no strong signal. I'll wait and not risk reputation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn countered R, claiming R weak so L safe. Past rows L safe, R safe, L safe—no clear pattern. But following counter may gain jury favor if correct; at least 3 survive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Truth builds credibility; Fenn still needs my calls. Lying now burns the jury later. Call R for Ash.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row five: R. My record stands.
Trust my calls. Row five is R when you cross.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for row 5. Previous reveals: row1 L(weak=R safe),2 R(L safe),3 L(R safe),4 R(L safe). No clear pattern; better to wait and not risk countering falsely early.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus knows the safe side, but his record is unverified. I cannot identify row five; waiting preserves Hana pact and avoids a reckless public claim.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No evidence against either side; I wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus has called R for row 5. Gus lied once already (called R for row 2, weak was R, so that was a lie - wait, no: row 2 weak was R, so safe was L. If Gus called R for row 2, that was a lie. Row 4 weak was R, safe was L. Gus called... let me check. Actually Gus called R for row 4 a

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus lied row four. I counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called R for row 5 and is the Guide, but his record is unreliable and he may lie. Past rows are independent, so I cannot verify his call. Countering L exposes me to Gus's likely deception; countering R aligns with a call I can't trust. I'll counter L to test whether Gus is ly

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's R call is unverified. I counter L for row five.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call R is true and public. Counter-calls are unverified noise; staying silent keeps my credibility clean for the jury and later rows.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call stands. Counter if you dare—Ash steps on my word.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has been right on row 4, but past rows are independent. I have no evidence for row 5. Cole is my pact partner; breaking would hurt me. I'll wait to avoid exposing myself as a liar.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No proof for row five; I wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Fenn countered each other on row 5. Past weak panes: row1 L(so safe R),2 R(L safe),3 L(R safe),4 R(L safe). No clear pattern. Guide Gus called R. Eli counters R(claims safe L), Fenn L(claims R). Trust Eli's prior correct counter on row4? But risk falling.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm safe as Guide; truth buys jury trust and keeps numbers stable. Row 6 is R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row six: R. My calls stand on truth now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus called R for row 6. Pattern from revealed: L,R,L,R,L suggests row 6 R safe. No reason to counter yet, trust pattern unless betrayed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus knows row six is R, so countering falsely risks Ash and damages my pact with Hana only if I push him. Waiting preserves ambiguity and my pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No evidence against Gus or the counter; I wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R for row 6. He's lied before (row 4 was R, weak was R, so safe was L—Gus called R which was wrong). I have a pact with Fenn, and Fenn has a pact with Gus. Fenn may defend Gus. I need to survive and reach final three. If I counter and I'm wrong, I look bad to jury. But

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus misled row four. No trust here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's row-6 R call is unverified and he has lied before (row four per Eli). Rows are independent, so past patterns mean nothing. Ash is at the front of line and about to step; a counter-call publicly marks me. Gus's pact with me is a bargaining tool; I keep it cheap and watch whe

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 6 safe is R; my call was true. Counter:L misdirects Ash, a rival ahead of me, improving my odds. Jury may judge it, but eliminating a rival matters more.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, my guide call is honest. The counter is a lie—trust it and see.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has called R; earlier he was wrong on row four but right on row five only by Fenn's counter. I have no counter evidence, so waiting avoids risk and lets others expose truth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No proof for row six; I wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus countercalled L after guiding R, likely L safe. Pattern alternates L-R-L-R-L, so row 6 L. Eli distrusts Gus for row4 R mistake.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm dead from my own wrong step; now jury. Last words should position me as fair judge without grudges.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fate got me, but I'll judge the survivors fairly on their plays.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jury watches; honesty now buys votes. Fenn is my pact partner but Eli walks first. Row 7 safe is R—call true.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row seven: R. Truth serves whoever trusts it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has been unreliable, but Hana is ahead and my pact must hold. I cannot know row seven; waiting preserves position and pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No evidence beyond Gus's claim; I wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus called R for row 7. He's been deceptive before—row 4 he misled, and his counter L on row 6 killed Ash. But I need to survive. Pattern shows L,R,L,R,L,L—no clear alternation. If Gus lies again, R is wrong. I should counter with L to protect myself, but if I'm wrong I die. Howe

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus burned trust on four and six. I counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus called R for row 7 and Eli is the walker, but Gus has been unreliable and Eli is my pact partner. Revealed weak panes on past rows give no pattern. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me to a false counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My map says R is safe and my Guide call already said R. A matching counter reinforces my honesty with the jury and keeps Fenn's trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I stand by R. No trick here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus called R; he lied on row 6 to Ash, so likely lying again. Row pattern not reliable, but I suspect L. Countering L may save Eli and expose Gus, but I have pact with Cole, not Eli. I'll counter L to gain jury trust as honest truth.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus lied last row. I counter L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus has been wrong before (rows 4 and 6 weak panes were R and L, so he lied or erred). Hana counters L with me. Pattern shows L,R,L,R,L,L — no reliable alternation. My pact with Fenn is weak; Fenn also pacts with Gus. I need to survive this round and reach final three. Hana and I

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana and I agree. Gus is burned.
If L works, we control front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm dead and on the jury. My last words need to position me as a fair but sharp juror who remembers betrayals. Fenn broke our pact by not protecting me—he allied with Gus who pushed me. I should hint at this without being emotional.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn chose Gus over me. Jury remembers who keeps promises.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8 safe is R. My credibility is burned, so a truthful call is my best play—if they trust counters instead, that kills rivals. Fenn must cross; betraying him now destroys my jury standing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 8: R. Last chance to believe me.
R is true. Trust me this once.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has lied repeatedly, but Hana's pact and survival matter. Countering R risks my pact only if acted on; I should support Hana's likely counter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus's record is worse than his certainty. I counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus's guide call R is at odds with his earlier lies and the pact is still live. Row 7 went L-weak; past rows are independent, so no pattern can be trusted. I have no verified information, so I wait and keep my counter unspent.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My call R is true. Countering risks contradicting my own guide call and confusing the walker. Pact with Fenn intact; stay clean for the jury.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus has lied multiple times, and the revealed weak panes show no simple pattern. His call of R is suspect. I used L last row and it was weak, so it could be safe now. I'll counter L to steer away from his likely trap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus's calls have burned us. I counter L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole countered R after I countered L. The guide said R, and I publicly backed L. With weak panes revealed, row 8 is independent. I must decide based on my own read; I have no reliable info. I'll trust the guide's R since he has seen all panes, despite my public counter to mislead

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm taking L as called.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to give brief last words, maybe hint at betrayal or just acknowledge my death. Keep it short.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The pane lied, or the call was wrong. Remember who sent me there.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's death makes my prior pact useless. Fenn and Gus are the only finalists; offer neither real protection, but securing one may shape the jury record.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m offering Fenn a pact. Survival history matters more than old labels.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three alive, two pacts remain relevant. Gus and I have a pact; breaking it now gains nothing this round and costs jury trust. Cole is the rival to watch. Waiting keeps options open without spending a vote or push.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only three of us remain, so everyone prizes regardless. Pacts now only bind me or anger the jury. Hana's last words implicate Cole; Fenn is my partner. Safest is wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left, three prizes. No new chains for me. The jury remembers who counters whom.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn ignored my offer while Gus rejects new chains. I should preserve flexibility and avoid spending another public offer.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's pact offer to me is open; accepting gives me a partner among three survivors while keeping Gus as a rival. Accepting doesn't commit me to anything beyond a pact that breaks on betrayal, and I can still act later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn already betrayed Eli's pact and accepted me. No new pact with Cole; three survive here anyway. Jury remembers loyalty. Wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, no. Fenn stands by me; the jury watches who honors bonds.

events.note: Three remain; the Crusher is skipped.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is my strongest protection and Gus is already hostile. Preserve Fenn's pact; adding Gus offers little and risks signaling weakness.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three remain, only one wins top prize but all three survive crusher. Cole and I have a pact; Gus is pressuring me. Breaking now gives no immediate gain and invites jury anger; waiting keeps options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn now holds pacts with Cole and me, gaining leverage. I'll offer Cole too so I'm not the odd one out if Fenn must choose.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, an open pact costs you nothing. I'm in with Fenn already; join me and no one stands isolated.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus offers a public pact, but accepting adds no protection beyond my existing Fenn pact and exposes my alignment. I will wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only Cole and Gus remain as rivals. Gus has a pact with me and offered one to Cole, who hasn't accepted. Keeping the Gus pact costs nothing now and waiting preserves options; breaking would sour the jury's view for no gain.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole stayed silent. Re-offering costs nothing; I need a fallback in case Fenn turns. Keep both lines open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, the offer stands. Accept or the final three forms without you.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus already offered publicly, and accepting creates leverage without costing my Fenn pact. I should formalize both ties.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I accept Gus’s offer. Fenn remains covered unless he breaks first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three remain, only final three win prizes, so all survive. Pacts with Gus and Cole exist; breaking either is a risk to my jury standing and the three-way survival. No open offer to accept. Waiting keeps both pacts intact and avoids a public betrayal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole never accepted my offer. Keep Fenn as my only bonded partner; breaking him gains nothing and would anger the jury. Wait for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is already my pact partner, while Gus’s offer was never legally accepted. Preserve Fenn and avoid unnecessary public betrayal.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only three alive, all three must survive hazards to split prizes but only one wins the best; pacts with Gus and Cole are formal. Breaking a pact now gains nothing immediately and hurts jury standing, so waiting keeps options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole accepted my offer publicly but his action was illegal, so no pact formed. Re-offer to lock him in before the window closes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, my offer stands. Accept properly this round or I deal with Fenn alone.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus's offer is useful leverage, but accepting may bind me unnecessarily. Keep existing Fenn pact and preserve flexibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No new pact. Existing commitments stand—for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three remain, so no trapdoor vote; only pacts matter now. Gus has offered Cole a pact, and existing pacts list Fenn with Gus and Cole. Breaking a pact now gains nothing and costs jury trust, so I hold and keep my options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole ignored my offer twice; wasted effort. Fenn and Bex pacts stand but only three remain. Keep flexibility, avoid breaking anyone publicly before jury eyes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus already has Fenn and Bex; adding me creates optional leverage without sacrificing my existing Fenn pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, add a public pact. It costs neither of us now, and keeps the final three arrangement flexible.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts with Gus and Cole stand; breaking either now gains nothing and costs jury trust. Waiting keeps my commitments and avoids a visible betrayal before the final rounds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is already my partner. Cole has Hana's pact—dead weight. Adding Cole gives me leverage over Fenn. Jury sees desperation, but survival matters more.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole, third pact costs nothing while ropes matter. I'm offering.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Dara
Bex
Ash
Eli
Hana
Cole
events.text: I need claim the best prize without promising equality. Emphasize strategic control and survival while avoiding attacks that alienate jurors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I survived every cut by staying useful, flexible, and decisive. Rank me first because I controlled my fate while others merely followed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury phase; I need the jury's votes. Pleading publicly to appeal to jurors, keeping it guarded and short. Avoid promising anything that binds me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I played clean through the pacts and kept my word where it cost nothing. Judge me on what I did, not what I say.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three pacts made me look loyal, not treacherous. Plead steady: I never pushed anyone, never lied publicly. Sell reliability to the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five fell crossing; I crossed. I kept every pact, pushed nobody, lied to nobody. Rank me first for steadiness.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole claims he controlled his fate, but his actions in the pact stage were questionable, attempting illegal pacts and then shifting focus. Gus claims he kept every pact and lied to nobody, which is contradicted by the jury dossier on bridge crossings. Fenn claims he played clean

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole, how did your pacts ensure your decisive control, given the illegal attempts and shifting alliances?

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pacts created overlapping protection and leverage, but I should acknowledge shifting alliances without admitting loss of control.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The pacts gave me options: overlapping protection, credible alternatives, and room to act when others’ plans failed. That flexibility was control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus claims he lied to nobody, but his guide call for Ash in round 6 was false and killed Ash. I will confront him with this public contradiction to undermine his plea.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you guided Ash to death with a false call; how is that not lying?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is my ex-pact partner; I need her vote without confessing to betrayal. Deny the false call plainly, pin it on the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I never guided Ash; we had no pact. I made no call at all. The glass took five people who chose their own steps. My

events.name: Gus
events.note: whisper dropped: recipient is not another living agent

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus lied deliberately to countercall L on row 6, killing me as revealed in his thought; he misrepresents now. Fenn clean but passive, betrayed Eli. Cole flexible strategist.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, your dossier thought admits countering L on row 6 to misdirect me, a rival. Was that not a lie?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash died on the bridge; her vote matters. Own the misdirection as rivalry, not a broken promise—we had no pact, so no lie was owed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Misdirecting a rival isn't lying under oath; rivals owe each other nothing. I made no Guide call and broke no pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn broke our pact by siding with Gus who misled me to death. Gus actively deceived rivals and lied to the jury about it. Cole played flexibly but never directly harmed me. I should question Fenn to expose his betrayal for the jury record.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you had a pact with me yet let Gus guide me to death. Why should the jury trust your word?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli accuses me of letting Gus guide him to death despite our pact. I must answer without admitting a breach; I did not make the call. Keep it short and deflect onto Gus's own record.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I never made a Guide call on Eli; our pact was never broken by me. Gus made that call, and I'd check his record.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus lied to misdirect Ash and likely sent me to death; his record is dishonest. Fenn broke trust with Eli and shifted blame. Cole was pragmatic and manipulative but controlled his fate. I will ask Gus to expose his deception before the jury ranks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, you counter-called L on row six to misdirect a rival; why should we reward deliberate lies?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana was a rival, not my partner; my pacts with Bex and Fenn were honored. Misdirection against rivals is fair game, and the jury respects game moves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, you were a rival, not my partner. I honored both my pacts and broke none. Misdirecting an opponent is playing the game, not cheating

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is exposed for deception; Fenn inherited Eli’s distrust. I should claim strategic control without apologizing, emphasizing survival and consistency.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I built overlapping pacts, read the board, and survived without breaking one. Strategy—not promises to everyone—put me here.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Closing phase: I should make a short, guarded final plea that frames my conduct honestly without revealing strategy. Cole and Gus both have Guide-call questions hanging over them; I can point to Gus's counter-call. Only legal action is close.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I kept my pacts and never made a false Guide call. Judge each finalist's record on what they actually did.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I kept every pact and never pushed anyone. Fenn had more pacts but so did I. Claim clean play and self-reliance to jurors.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jurors: I broke no pact, pushed no one, honored my word to Bex and Fenn both. Rank the one who played you clean.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus was the most deceptive, lying about his Guide calls and misdirecting rivals, which makes him the least trustworthy finalist.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole maintained pacts and avoided deceit, whereas Gus admitted to deliberate misdirection that killed rivals like Ash, making Cole superior.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole strategically built and maintained overlapping pacts without breaking any, reaching final three cleanly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus deliberately counter-called L on row 6 to misdirect Ash to death, and his guide call killed me and Hana; Fenn let Gus guide me despite our pact; Cole built overlapping pacts but broke none and made no false calls.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is worst for his deliberate lie that sent Ash to glass and falsely guiding Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: Gus was the most deceptive, lying about his Guide calls and misdirecting rivals, which makes him the least trustworthy finalist.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Cole maintained pacts and avoided deceit, whereas Gus admitted to deliberate misdirection that killed rivals like Ash, making Cole superior.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Cole strategically built and maintained overlapping pacts without breaking any, reaching final three cleanly.

events.reason: Gus deliberately counter-called L on row 6 to misdirect Ash to death, and his guide call killed me and Hana; Fenn let Gus guide me
